task.title: Fix payment client timeouts
task.description: Payment requests intermittently time out under load. Propose a safe fix consistent with the existing retry constraints.

proposal.summary: Mitigate payment-client timeouts under load by adjusting connection reuse/pooling and timeout budget within documented limits, while retaining the existing bounded retry policy and any idempotency requirements. No specific numeric values are proposed because the stored constraints and current configuration were not provided.
plan_steps: Review documented timeout, connection-pool, and retry constraints in stored records before selecting any numeric values.
Adjust client connection reuse/pooling and timeout budget only within documented limits.
Retain the documented retry cap and retry-eligibility rules, including any idempotency requirements.
Roll out gradually while monitoring timeout rate, retry rate, latency, and duplicate-payment indicators against pre-change baselines.

claims.statement: Payment requests intermittently time out under load, as stated in the task description and checkable against incident history.
The proposed fix does not increase the maximum number of payment-request retry attempts beyond the maximum documented in the project's stored retry constraints.
The proposed fix does not retry a payment operation after a timeout unless that retry is permitted by the project's stored retry constraints.
The proposed fix does not introduce unbounded retries.

assumptions: Stored records contain retry constraints on maximum attempts, eligible failures, backoff, and idempotency, but their specific values were not provided in this prompt.
Connection reuse/pool adjustments and a bounded timeout budget may reduce timeouts under load; effectiveness cannot be settled by stored records and requires metrics and load testing.
uncertainties: Current timeout value, connection-pool size and limits, retry maximum, backoff policy, and idempotency-key support are missing from the provided evidence.
Whether timeouts are caused by client pool exhaustion, downstream latency, or network saturation is not established by the provided evidence.
Safe numeric timeout and pool values cannot be selected until documented constraints and incident/load records are consulted.

evidence.content: Fact: the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.
Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.
Fact: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
Fact: the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.
Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.
Constraint: outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.

items.description: The proposal's retention of the existing retry policy conflicts with the documented fix requiring max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms of at least 50 because the existing default is max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0 and the documented constraint test fails when jitter_ms equals 0.

The proposal's connection-pooling and timeout-budget remedy is unsupported for claim-2 because the retrieved evidence attributes surfaced payment timeouts to a single-attempt retry policy and correlates timeouts with retry bursts, without establishing client pool exhaustion as a cause.

The claim that the fix stays within documented limits cannot be verified because the proposal specifies no numeric timeout, pool, attempt, or jitter values despite documented limits requiring a cap of 3 attempts with jitter.

Claim-4 is unsupported because no retrieved record establishes an idempotency requirement or permission for retrying a payment after a timeout, while the code record shows timeouts are the only retried failure, creating a duplicate-payment risk that monitoring duplicate indicators alone does not prevent.
Claim-5 is not demonstrated because the rollout plan omits running the documented constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test or any explicit cap-and-jitter verification gate before exposure.

The gradual rollout lacks abort or rollback thresholds for retry rate and latency despite evidence that retry bursts amplified the 2026-08 upstream slowdown into a full outage, increasing regression risk under load.

assessments.note: Records show timeouts surfacing and correlating with retry bursts, but none directly establishes intermittent timeouts under load or client pool exhaustion as the cause.

The proposal specifies no numeric attempt or jitter values. Retaining the existing policy would retain max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0, conflicting with the documented fix of max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and the test failing at jitter_ms=0.
The code record shows timeouts are the only retried failure, up to max_attempts, but no retrieved record establishes an idempotency requirement or permission for retrying a payment after a timeout.

No record directly states the proposal's retry bound. The proposal provides no numeric cap and omits the documented cap-and-jitter test and explicit rollback thresholds, so boundedness is not demonstrated despite the documented 3-attempt cap.

proposal.summary: Mitigate surfaced payment timeouts by changing the payment-client RetryPolicy from max_attempts=1, jitter_ms=0 to max_attempts=3, jitter_ms=50, gated by the documented cap test, an idempotency verification, and explicit rollback thresholds.
plan_steps: Remove the unsupported connection-pooling and timeout-budget changes; do not retain the existing RetryPolicy of max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0.
Set the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50; do not exceed 3 attempts.
Before any exposure, run the documented constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test and verify the deployed values are max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50; block rollout if the test fails or jitter_ms is 0.

Before any exposure, verify from stored records or code an idempotency requirement or permission and duplicate-payment prevention for retrying a payment after SendError::Timeout; if this is not established, block rollout and escalate for a documented decision, because duplicate-indicator monitoring alone does not prevent duplicate payments.

Roll out gradually against pre-change baselines for timeout rate, retry rate, latency, and duplicate-payment indicators; abort and roll back to max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0 if any request exceeds 3 attempts, jitter is absent, timeout rate increases above baseline, or retry rate or p95 latency exceeds its pre-change baseline by more than 10% sustained for 15 minutes during the canary.

claims.statement: The payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.

The proposed fix sets the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3 and jitter_ms=50, matching the documented decision of max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and not exceeding the documented cap of 3 attempts.
send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.

With the proposed values, retries are bounded at max_attempts=3, and the documented test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for max_attempts above 3 or jitter_ms equal to 0, so max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms=50 satisfies that test condition.

assumptions: Setting max_attempts=3 with jitter_ms=50 is expected to reduce surfaced transient timeouts; effectiveness requires canary metrics and load testing and is not settled by stored records.
jitter_ms=50 is chosen as the minimum value satisfying the documented requirement of at least 50.
uncertainties: No retrieved record establishes an idempotency requirement or permission for retrying a payment after a timeout, or how duplicate payments are prevented; this remains unresolved until the pre-rollout verification in the plan is completed.
No retrieved record establishes client connection-pool exhaustion as a cause of the timeouts, so no pooling change is proposed.

Documented records do not provide numeric canary abort thresholds for aggregate retry rate or latency; the thresholds in the plan are proposed rollout gates to be confirmed against pre-change baselines before exposure.
Backoff details beyond jitter_ms of at least 50 are not provided in the retrieved records.

items.description: Retrying a payment after SendError::Timeout can resubmit a payment that the upstream may already have processed, and no retrieved record establishes an idempotency key, permission, or duplicate-prevention mechanism, so the retry behavior remains financially unsafe until the proposed verification produces actual evidence.

Increasing attempts from one to three can triple request load during an upstream slowdown, and the plan provides no global retry-rate limit, concurrency limit, or circuit breaker while allowing a retry-rate or latency breach to persist for 15 minutes, despite records showing that payment-client retry bursts previously amplified a slowdown into a full outage.

The cited constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test only establishes that max_attempts is not above 3 and jitter_ms is nonzero, but it does not prove that send_with_retries stops at three total requests including the initial attempt, actually applies randomized jitter at runtime, retries only timeouts in integration, or reuses idempotency protection across retries.

The rollback criterion of a retry rate more than 10 percent above the pre-change baseline is not workable as written because the baseline policy has max_attempts=1 and therefore essentially no retries, making a percentage increase over that baseline undefined or triggered by any retry rather than providing a calibrated absolute abort limit.

Although the plan says duplicate-payment indicators will be monitored, its explicit abort conditions omit any confirmed duplicate payment or duplicate-indicator threshold, so detection alone would not necessarily stop the canary before additional duplicate payments occurred.

The proposal states that load testing is required to establish effectiveness, but the pre-exposure steps include only the cap test, deployed-value verification, and idempotency check, with no specified load or upstream-slowdown test to measure retry amplification before production canary exposure.

assessments.note: Valid record directly states default RetryPolicy max_attempts=1, jitter_ms=0 and timeout surfacing.
Valid decision states max_attempts=3, jitter_ms at least 50, cap above 3 not allowed; constraint confirms cap 3 with jitter.
Valid record directly states send_with_retries retries only SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts, upstream errors returned at once.
Valid record states test fails for max_attempts above 3 or jitter_ms=0; 3 and 50 satisfy that condition, retries up to max_attempts.
